records.name: Linear task workflow
records.workflow: create task → sort it → set its priority → choose an owner → plan the work → review it → complete it.
records.states: new task waiting to be sorted, planned for later, work started, work blocked, task canceled, duplicate task, work completed.
records.pattern: People can see a lot of work at once, update it quickly, and stay on the same screen.
records.recreation: A keyboard-friendly work queue that shows what needs attention, who owns it, and what happens next.

records.name: Stripe payment and failure recovery
records.workflow: set up the account → start a payment → confirm the customer's identity → payment succeeds or fails → send the money, issue a refund, or handle a dispute.
records.states: account setup incomplete, payment waiting, payment succeeded, payment failed, money refunded, charge disputed, bank payout delayed.
records.pattern: A timeline shows what happened to the money, while clear actions tell the team how to fix a problem.
records.recreation: A payment timeline that explains failures and gives the team a clear way to recover.

records.name: Airbnb reservation
records.workflow: search for a place → narrow the results → open a listing → check dates and rules → review the full price → book the stay → prepare for the trip.
records.states: dates unavailable, waiting for the host, payment failed, booking canceled, trip in progress, help requested.
records.pattern: Strong photos build interest, while clear prices, rules, and reviews help people feel safe booking.
records.recreation: A booking journey that shows every fee and makes a failed payment easy to fix.

records.name: Uber ride request
records.workflow: enter a destination → see the price and wait time → request a ride → find a driver → wait for the driver → take the trip → pay → rate the ride or get help.
records.states: finding your location, searching for a driver, driver found, driver arriving, trip in progress, trip completed, ride canceled, safety help needed.
records.pattern: Each screen focuses on what is happening now and the one decision the rider needs to make.
records.recreation: A service request where the main button changes as the job moves from request to completion.

records.name: Instacart item replacement
records.workflow: add groceries to the cart → choose what should happen when an item is missing → shopper suggests a replacement → customer approves the change → deliver the replacement or issue a refund.
records.states: item unavailable, replacement suggested, waiting for approval, replacement approved, part of the order delivered, refund issued, delivery late.
records.pattern: A messy supply problem becomes a small choice the customer can understand and approve.
records.recreation: A replacement choice that shows the price difference and lets the customer approve it or ask for a refund.

records.name: Duolingo daily lesson
records.workflow: choose a daily goal → take a short lesson → see whether each answer is right → receive a progress reward → get a daily reminder → return for the next lesson.
records.states: first lesson, answer correct, answer incorrect, daily streak at risk, daily goal met, no tries left, paid plan offered.
records.pattern: Short lessons, visible progress, and quick rewards give people a reason to return tomorrow.
records.recreation: A five-minute lesson that helps people recover from mistakes and offers an upgrade without getting in the way.

records.name: Rover pet care booking
records.workflow: describe the care needed → search for caregivers → compare profiles, reviews, and schedules → ask a question → book the service → receive updates → leave a review.
records.states: no caregivers found, question sent, booking requested, booking accepted, care coming up, care in progress, problem reported, care completed.
records.pattern: Profiles, schedules, messages, and proof of good care help people trust a stranger with their pet.
records.recreation: A service booking journey that clearly shows the change from asking a question to having a confirmed booking.

records.name: Shopify order shipping
records.workflow: receive the order → reserve the items → prepare the package → buy a label and ship it → track the package → deliver it, accept a return, or issue a refund.
records.states: not shipped, partly shipped, on the way, delivered, held, returned, refunded.
records.pattern: Each order shows the next action and calls attention to anything that may delay delivery.
records.recreation: An order board that puts delayed and risky orders ahead of routine ones.

records.name: Mobbin product journey library
records.workflow: choose a device or topic → search or browse → open a product journey → inspect each screen → save or compare the example.
records.states: browsing, filters applied, no search results, journey opened, screenshot enlarged, item saved, sign-in required.
records.pattern: A connected set of screens teaches more than a single attractive screenshot because it shows how the experience works.
records.recreation: A reference library that connects screenshots in order and explains what each screen is doing.

records.name: Awwwards project gallery
records.workflow: browse the gallery → narrow the results or open a project → try its movement and interactions → read about the project or the team behind it.
records.states: gallery open, pointer over an item, project loading, moving between pages, project opened, visiting another site, movement reduced for accessibility.
records.pattern: Strong visual effects work better when people can still tell where they are and where to go next.
records.recreation: A small gallery with lively movement, clear navigation, and a simpler version for people who reduce motion.

records.name: Intercom support assignment
records.workflow: receive a customer message → collect the customer history → answer automatically or choose a support person → reply → pause it or ask another team for help → close or reopen it.
records.states: automatic greeting sent, customer waiting, support person assigned, conversation paused, another team asked to help, conversation closed, conversation reopened.
records.pattern: Automation and support staff work from the same conversation, so customers do not have to repeat themselves.
records.recreation: A support inbox that shows the customer history, suggests a reply, assigns an owner, and lets the team pause or reopen a conversation.

records.name: Airtable form follow-up
records.workflow: publish the form → receive an answer → check that the answer is complete → save it → run the follow-up steps → assign the work or notify someone.
records.states: empty form, missing or incorrect answer, form submitted, repeated submission, follow-up steps running, follow-up failed, work assigned.
records.pattern: A simple form can collect clean information for a team without showing customers the internal system.
records.recreation: A public request form that creates an internal task, assigns an owner, and records every change.

records.name: Retool team work console
records.workflow: sign in → narrow the list → open an item → review the related information → make a change → confirm that it worked.
records.states: loading, information out of date, access denied, delete confirmation, change saved, change failed.
records.pattern: Even a complicated work tool can feel clear when the details and the available actions appear together.
records.recreation: A searchable work queue with record details, an approval button, and a history of changes.

records.name: Figma design review and handoff
records.workflow: start a design → try ideas → leave comments → revise the work → approve it → give it to the team building it → reuse its parts.
records.states: early draft, being edited, comment still open, comment addressed, waiting for review, alternate version created, reusable parts published.
records.pattern: People discuss the exact part of the design they mean, instead of moving the conversation to another tool.
records.recreation: A design review board with comments attached to specific items and a checklist for finishing the work.

records.name: ServiceTitan job completion
records.workflow: receive a service request → estimate the price → schedule the visit → send a technician → complete the work → add notes and photos → get approval → send the bill → follow up.
records.states: not scheduled, technician assigned, technician on the way, technician on site, approval needed, waiting for parts, work completed, ready to bill, problem found.
records.pattern: The office plan stays useful when field workers can report what actually happened on the job.
records.recreation: A completed-job review that points out missing time, notes, photos, approvals, or billing details.

records.name: Buildertrend construction project
records.workflow: receive a possible job → estimate the price → sign the contract → choose materials and finishes → set the schedule → track the budget → approve changes → build the project → finish the remaining small jobs → handle warranty work.
records.states: early draft, waiting for the client to choose, waiting for approval, work scheduled, work delayed, change requested, small job still unfinished, project complete.
records.pattern: Clients trust the project more when they can see progress, delays, decisions, and changes in one place.
records.recreation: A project closeout screen that shows changes, approvals, previous versions, and work that is still unfinished.

records.name: OpenTable reservation
records.workflow: choose a place and date → browse restaurants → narrow the results → open a restaurant → choose a time → confirm the booking → receive a reminder → visit or cancel.
records.states: no tables available, added to the waitlist, table held for a few minutes, booking confirmed, reminder sent, guest running late, booking canceled.
records.pattern: Available times come first. Restaurant details help people feel confident enough to book one.
records.recreation: A reservation picker that handles limited times, waitlists, confirmation, and cancellation clearly.

records.name: Wise international transfer
records.workflow: choose the two currencies → enter the amount to send → see the fee and amount the other person will receive → confirm who gets the money → pay → track the transfer.
records.states: price shown, identity check waiting, payment waiting, money moving, money delivered, transfer failed, money refunded.
records.pattern: People are more willing to send money when they see the fee, delivery time, and current progress clearly.
records.recreation: A money transfer tracker that shows the fee, delivery amount, current progress, and how to fix a failure.

records.name: Vercel software release
records.workflow: connect the code → start a release → build the website → read the build messages → check the preview → make it live or restore the previous version.
records.states: waiting to build, building, preview ready, build failed, build canceled, version made live, previous version restored.
records.pattern: A step-by-step timeline shows developers what the system is doing and what to try when a build fails.
records.recreation: A software release timeline that shows each build step, explains failures, links to the preview, and can restore the previous version.

records.name: Sentry error sorting
records.workflow: error arrives → group similar errors → inspect what happened → choose an owner → link the repair task → mark it fixed → check whether it returns.
records.states: new problem, problem happening again, problem ignored, owner assigned, repair task linked, problem fixed, problem returned after a fix.
records.pattern: A flood of errors becomes manageable when similar ones are grouped and each problem has an owner.
records.recreation: An error list that shows how often a problem happens, who owns it, and whether it came back after a fix.
